canonical_name: Viterbi / HMM decoder (compact C++ reference, Min Xu)
lineage: The Viterbi algorithm (1967) over a Hidden Markov Model (Rabiner 1989): find the most-likely hidden state path for an observation sequence by dynamic programming over the trellis; this is a small, tested C++ reference of the HMM + Viterbi decode
version: github.com/xukmin/viterbi master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)
entry_points: Viterbi decode over an HMM (states, transition, emission, observations) -> most-likely state path; the shipped test + main
upstream_docs: Viterbi, Error bounds for convolutional codes..., 1967
Rabiner, A Tutorial on Hidden Markov Models, 1989

human_capability_summary.built_to: recover the most-likely sequence of hidden states that produced an observed sequence, by dynamic programming over the HMM trellis (predict-then-max at each step)
human_capability_summary.pressure: the true state sequence is never observed, only noisy emissions; the number of possible paths is exponential in sequence length
human_capability_summary.success_means: the decoded path matches the true generating states on the test HMM; likelihood computed correctly

known_human_problem_solved: most-likely-path inference in a hidden Markov model (Viterbi)
human_environmental_pressure: hidden state, noisy/ambiguous emissions, exponential path space
human_failure_condition: a wrong transition/emission model yields a wrong decoded path -- a speech recogniser or gene finder built on it makes systematic errors
behavioral_entry_point: perturb the emission or transition probabilities, or make two states' emissions overlap, and watch the decoded path change; the shipped test is the oracle

versions_preserved.note: the richer historical GHMM (Baum-Welch training + forward-backward, MPI-MG, autotools C) is queued as a heavier same-lineage companion

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run viterbi-hmm-xukmin
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: recover the most-likely sequence of hidden states that produced an observed sequence, by dynamic programming over the HMM trellis (predict-then-max at each step)
